figures/umferdarmerki-enska-p010full-s00.reason: DELIBERATE CONSERVATIVE EXCLUSION, re-applied after B12 recovered this sign. Not an OCR defect: the label above is a correct reading of the page, taken at native resolution, and its entry stays in sign-label-corrections.json on purpose — a correct reading stays recorded even for a sign the deck does not ship, so the two files disagree by design. THE CROP: a grey carriageway with three short white blocks stepping up off a thin continuous line that runs the full width. THE PROBLEM: in-deck p010full-s004 ('Half-broken centre line with unbroken central line') depicts the SAME PHYSICAL MARKING — a solid line beside a broken one — differing only in dash-to-gap ratio (s004: four long blocks with narrow gaps over a thick band; s007: three short blocks with long gaps over a thin line) and NEITHER LABEL NAMES THAT DIFFERENCE. Contrast p010full-s003/s006, where 'Half-broken' versus 'Broken' maps directly onto long versus short dashes and the caption tells the learner what to look at. The two co-occur as options in two cards, so a learner can only score them by memorising crop artefacts, and the risk is grading a correct reading wrong — the exact defect B2 shipped. Cost of excluding: 2 sign cards. 'A missing card beats a wrong card' decides it. TO OVERTURN: delete this entry and rebuild; the label correction is already in place, so the sign returns with its correct reading and no other change is needed. Do that only if the pair is given captions that name the discriminator, or the app renders crops large enough to read dash geometry at a glance (currently 198x176). Related: FIXES.md C4 and B12's watch list.
